input.summary: 298 mapped relationships expose seven use-case chains blocked by compounding foundational gaps across Meridian's estate.
covers: Epic, Claims, CRM, and Analytics platform interdependencies
sources: MER-V3-EVID-REL-PROG series (DATA-FOUNDATION, API-MOD, PHI-IAM, EHR-CLIN, CONTACT-KNOW, FINOPS, AI-GOV, MSO, COPILOT-ADOPT)

story.meaning: Meridian's seven priority use cases share a single upstream dependency cluster — lakehouse foundation, identity spine, governance model, and semantic layer — none of which are certified.
story.observed: 72 active relationships and 226 candidates map Epic Clarity, Claims, Pharmacy, CRM, and SAS to use-case chains. Every chain terminates at one or more of the same four unresolved foundation gaps, creating a compounding blockade across all programs.
story.matters: Until the lakehouse foundation and governance operating model are certified, no downstream use case — AI automation, cost transparency, payment integrity, call center optimization, or provider quality — can advance past planning grade.
story.supports: Closing the four shared foundation gaps (medallion architecture, identity spine, semantic layer, governance model) unlocks all seven use cases simultaneously and is the highest-leverage investment decision on the board agenda.

findings: All seven Meridian use cases share the same four upstream blockers: no certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal governance model, and no certified semantic layer — resolving these in sequence unlocks the entire portfolio.

226 of 298 relationship rows remain candidate-grade, meaning the majority of system-to-use-case linkages are directional only; Epic Clarity, Claims, and SAS connections to AI and cost use cases carry the highest unresolved dependency risk.

The SAS analytics estate is the current production engine for payment integrity and cost analytics but has no governed model lineage, creating a regulatory and audit exposure that blocks both use cases from advancing regardless of lakehouse readiness.

Call center optimization is isolated from the lakehouse chain but carries its own four-gap stack — transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage — all unproven, making it the most self-contained but equally blocked workstream.

rows.label: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
rows.note: Medallion, identity spine, harmonization, and AWS/Databricks foundation all unresolved; blocks four downstream use cases

rows.label: Governed Data Foundation / AI-LLM
rows.note: No governance model, semantic layer, AI audit trail, or data quality rules; prerequisite for all AI programs

rows.label: Provider Quality & Cost Transparency
rows.note: Attribution, contract digitization, GL alignment, and measure fragmentation span both use cases across Epic and SQL Server marts

rows.label: Payment Integrity & Leakage
rows.note: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution, investigation workflow, and recovery tracking all unproven

rows.label: Call Center Optimization
rows.note: Transcript governance, real-time integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage all unproven; CRM and telephony ungoverned for analytics

chain: Epic Clarity + Epic Caboodle → Medallion Architecture (unproven) → Patient/Member Identity Spine (unproven) → Claims + Pharmacy Harmonization (unproven) → Unified Lakehouse
Unified Lakehouse → Formal Governance Model (absent) + Certified Semantic Layer (absent) → AI/LLM Automation + Cost Transparency + Provider Quality
SAS Analytics Estate → Governed Model Lineage (absent) → Payment Integrity + Leakage Reduction
Contact Center Telephony + CRM → Transcript Governance (absent) + Real-Time Integration (unproven) → Call Center Optimization
Provider Contract Repository → Contract Digitization (absent) + Attribution Certification (absent) → Cost Transparency + Provider Quality
relationships.note: Every use-case chain at Meridian converges on the same unresolved foundation layer. The lakehouse and governance gaps are not parallel workstreams — they are sequential prerequisites that gate the entire seven-use-case portfolio. Resolving them in order is the critical path.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture or patient/member identity spine
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse; blocks four downstream use cases that depend on a governed longitudinal patient view
gaps.needed: Epic Clarity and Caboodle medallion certification; Reltio MDM identity spine load; Claims and Pharmacy harmonization proof
gaps.handoff: CDAO and CIO must jointly own architecture certification gate before any lakehouse-dependent use case advances to build

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model or certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: All AI/LLM automation use cases; also blocks cost transparency, provider quality, and payment integrity from reaching audit-grade outputs
gaps.needed: Collibra or equivalent governance operating model stood up; dbt/Power BI semantic layer certified; AI audit trail instrumented
gaps.handoff: Chief Data Officer must own governance model delivery as a program gate; no AI use case should receive investment approval without this in place

gaps.missing: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction use case; investigation and recovery workflows cannot be evidenced without governed lineage
gaps.needed: SAS-to-Databricks lineage documentation; provider entity resolution via MDM; investigation workflow evidence captured
gaps.handoff: Health Plan Ops and Finance must co-own lineage governance; CFO sign-off required before leakage quantification is reported

gaps.missing: Transcript governance and real-time CRM integration unproven
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization; agent-assist and next-best-action cannot be deployed without governed transcript and member identity linkage
gaps.needed: Transcript governance policy approved; Genesys-to-Salesforce real-time integration certified; intent taxonomy validated
gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer and CIO must co-own contact center data governance; member identity linkage requires MDM coordination with CDAO

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form; attribution ownership unproven
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases; margin and quality outputs cannot be trusted without contract and attribution certification
gaps.needed: Provider contract digitization into governed repository; attribution model ownership assigned and certified; GL-claims calendar alignment proven
gaps.handoff: CFO and Chief Medical Officer must jointly resolve attribution and contract digitization; Network Contracting owns the contract repository input

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Relationship Bundle
evidence.facts: Four system-to-use-case relationships mapped: Epic Clarity/Caboodle and Claims/Pharmacy to lakehouse. All four carry active gaps — medallion architecture, identity spine, harmonization, and AWS/Databricks foundation readiness.
evidence.fields: use_case, risk_or_gap, affected_systems, confidence, active_candidate_status, metric_boundary
evidence.supports: Lakehouse use case is the foundational prerequisite chain; all four gaps must close before downstream use cases can advance
evidence.missing: No certified medallion architecture loaded; no identity spine evidence; no harmonization proof; AWS/Databricks foundation aspirational only

evidence.name: Governed Data Foundation / AI-LLM Relationship Bundle
evidence.facts: Four relationships map Epic Clarity, SQL Server marts, and SAS estate to AI/LLM governance use case. Gaps: no formal governance model, no semantic layer, no AI audit trail, no data quality rules.
evidence.fields: use_case, risk_or_gap, affected_systems, confidence, active_candidate_status, metric_boundary
evidence.supports: Governance and semantic layer are cross-cutting prerequisites; their absence blocks all seven use cases from reaching audit or decision grade
evidence.missing: No governance operating model; no Collibra or equivalent certification; no AI audit trail instrumentation evidenced

evidence.name: Call Center Optimization Relationship Bundle
evidence.facts: Four relationships map Genesys telephony, Salesforce CRM, and Claims platform to call center optimization. Gaps: transcript governance, real-time integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage all unproven.
evidence.fields: use_case, risk_or_gap, affected_systems, confidence, active_candidate_status, metric_boundary
evidence.supports: Call center optimization is self-contained from the lakehouse chain but equally blocked; four independent gaps must close before agent-assist can be deployed
evidence.missing: No transcript governance policy; no real-time Genesys-to-Salesforce integration proof; no certified intent taxonomy; member identity linkage not evidenced

evidence.name: Provider Quality & Cost Transparency Relationship Bundle
evidence.facts: Eight relationships map Epic Caboodle/Clarity, Tableau, Power BI, Provider Contract Repository, Claims, and GL to provider quality and cost transparency use cases. Gaps span attribution, contract digitization, measure fragmentation, and GL alignment.
evidence.fields: use_case, risk_or_gap, affected_systems, confidence, active_candidate_status, metric_boundary
evidence.supports: Provider contract digitization and attribution certification are the shared critical-path items for both use cases; neither can reach decision grade without them
evidence.missing: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form; attribution ownership unassigned; GL-claims calendar alignment unproven; measure logic fragmented across Tableau and Power BI

evidence.name: Program-Level Change Relationship Bundle (PROG series)
evidence.type: Program change linkage mapping — synthetic planning-grade
evidence.facts: Program-level relationships cover DATA-FOUNDATION, API-MOD, PHI-IAM, EHR-CLIN, CONTACT-KNOW, FINOPS, AI-GOV, MSO, COPILOT-ADOPT, and SNOW-AI. Systems include MuleSoft, Apigee, Okta, CyberArk, GitHub Copilot, ServiceNow, and Workday.
evidence.supports: Program-level relationships confirm that API modernization, PHI/IAM controls, and AI governance programs are all in-flight but none are certified as complete; they are enabling conditions for use-case advancement
evidence.missing: No program completion certification; FHIR streaming, integration observability, and audit automation are aspirational; no PHI audit logging certification evidenced

evidence.name: Candidate Relationship Pool
evidence.facts: 226 of 298 relationship rows are candidate-grade, meaning system-to-use-case linkages are directional and not yet evidence-backed. High confidence assigned to 228 rows; medium to 70. Candidate pool includes all seven use-case domains.
evidence.supports: The large candidate pool signals that relationship mapping is structurally complete but evidence closure is the outstanding work; confidence ratings are high but active status is low
evidence.missing: Evidence closure required for 226 candidate rows before any relationship can be promoted to active and used to gate investment decisions
